passages.title: Shade for the City
passages.text: On a summer afternoon, a city block lined with mature trees can be several degrees cooler than a nearby block covered in asphalt and concrete. Scientists call the broader pattern the urban heat island effect: dark, hard surfaces absorb sunlight during the day and release that stored heat slowly at night, so cities often stay warmer than the surrounding countryside long after sunset. Trees counter this in two ways. Their leaves shade the ground, keeping sunlight from reaching heat-absorbing pavement, and they release water vapor through tiny pores in their leaves, a process that cools the surrounding air much as sweat cools skin. Planting trees is not a perfect solution, however. Young trees need years to grow a canopy wide enough to matter, and they require regular watering during their first summers. Even so, many city planners now treat trees less as decoration and more as public health infrastructure, especially in neighborhoods where older residents are most vulnerable to dangerous heat.

passages.title: Riverside Community Clinic: Seasonal Flu Vaccine Days
passages.text:
Walk-in flu vaccinations will be offered every Tuesday and Thursday from October 7 through November 20, between 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. No appointment is needed on these days. Patients who prefer a scheduled time may book an appointment for any weekday by calling the front desk; appointments are available through December 19.

Please bring a photo ID and your insurance card. Patients without insurance can receive the vaccine at no cost through the clinic's community program, but they should arrive at least 15 minutes early to complete a short enrollment form.

Some children under 9 years old who are receiving a flu vaccine for the first time need two doses given at least four weeks apart. Parents should ask the nurse at the first visit whether a second dose is required.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

choices.A: Asphalt and concrete should be removed from cities to prevent heat-related illness.
choices.B: Trees can lower urban temperatures, and planners increasingly value them as a health resource despite their limitations.
choices.C: Young trees require frequent watering during their first summers.
choices.D: Cities are warmer than rural areas only during summer afternoons.

questions.explanation: The passage explains how trees cool cities, admits their limits, and ends by noting that planners now see them as public health infrastructure; choice B covers all of this. Choice C is a true supporting detail, but it is too narrow to be the main idea.

questions.stem: Why does the author compare the release of water vapor by leaves to the way "sweat cools skin"?

choices.A: To argue that trees and humans regulate their temperature in exactly the same way
choices.B: To shift the focus of the passage from cities to human health
choices.C: To suggest that the cooling effect of trees is too small to matter
choices.D: To explain an unfamiliar process by relating it to a familiar one

questions.explanation: The comparison helps readers picture evaporative cooling by linking it to an everyday experience. It is an analogy, not a claim that the two processes are identical, so choice A overstates it.

questions.stem: Based on the passage, the author would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: A city tree-planting program is more likely to succeed if it includes a plan for watering new trees.
choices.B: Planting young trees will cool a neighborhood almost immediately.
choices.C: The urban heat island effect disappears once the sun sets.
choices.D: Trees in cities are valuable mainly for their appearance.

questions.explanation: The author notes that young trees need regular watering in their first summers, so a program that plans for watering fits the author's view. Choices B, C, and D are each contradicted directly by the passage (trees take years, heat is released at night, and trees are more than decoration).

questions.stem: According to the notice, what should a patient without insurance do to receive a free flu vaccine?

choices.A: Call the front desk to book an appointment in advance
choices.B: Bring proof of income to the clinic
choices.C: Arrive at least 15 minutes early to complete an enrollment form
choices.D: Visit the clinic only on a Tuesday

questions.explanation: The notice states that uninsured patients should arrive at least 15 minutes early to fill out a short enrollment form. Nothing in the notice mentions proof of income or limits these patients to Tuesdays.

questions.stem: A patient wants a flu vaccine on Monday, December 8. Based on the notice, what should the patient do?

choices.A: Walk in to the clinic any time between 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.
choices.B: Call the front desk to schedule an appointment
choices.C: Wait until the following Tuesday and walk in
choices.D: Go to a different clinic, because vaccines are no longer offered after November 20

questions.explanation: Walk-in days end on November 20, but appointments can be booked for any weekday through December 19, and December 8 is a Monday in that window. Choice D is the common error: only walk-in service ends on November 20.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 + 2/3?
questions.explanation: Use the common denominator 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, so the sum is 17/12 = 1 5/12. Choice A comes from incorrectly adding the numerators and the denominators.

questions.stem: After a 20% discount, a pair of nursing shoes costs $36.00. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 80% of the original, so 0.80 × P = 36 and P = 36 ÷ 0.80 = $45.00. Choice B is the common mistake of adding 20% of the sale price instead of working backward from 80%.

questions.stem: Solve for x: 3(x − 4) + 5 = 2x + 7
questions.explanation: Distribute: 3x − 12 + 5 = 2x + 7, so 3x − 7 = 2x + 7. Subtract 2x and add 7 to get x = 14. Choice B results from forgetting to multiply the 4 by 3.

questions.stem: A medication is ordered at 5 mg per kilogram of body weight. The patient weighs 154 lb. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how many milligrams should the patient receive?
questions.explanation: First convert pounds to kilograms: 154 ÷ 2.2 = 70 kg. Then multiply by the dose: 70 × 5 = 350 mg. Choice C skips the conversion, and choice D multiplies by 2.2 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: A student's quiz scores are 82, 90, 75, 90, and 88. What is the median score?
questions.explanation: Put the scores in order (75, 82, 88, 90, 90); the middle value is 88. Choice A is the mean, choice B is the mode, and choice D is the range.

questions.stem: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle contracts and pushes oxygenated blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and on to the body. The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood into the pulmonary artery, and the atria only move blood into the ventricles.

questions.stem: In which organ does most absorption of nutrients into the bloodstream take place?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is lined with villi and microvilli that greatly increase its surface area, making it the main site of nutrient absorption. The large intestine mainly absorbs water and electrolytes, a common source of confusion.

questions.stem: In the nephron, blood is first filtered at which structure?
questions.explanation: The glomerulus is a capillary cluster where blood pressure forces water and small solutes into Bowman's capsule, forming the filtrate. The loop of Henle, distal tubule, and collecting duct act later, adjusting the filtrate through reabsorption and secretion.

questions.stem: In a species of beetle, the allele for a shiny shell (S) is completely dominant over the allele for a dull shell (s). Two heterozygous beetles (Ss × Ss) are crossed. What percentage of the offspring are expected to have dull shells?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives SS, Ss, Ss, and ss; only ss (1 of 4) shows the recessive dull phenotype, so 25%. Choice C is the percentage with shiny shells, not dull ones.

questions.stem: Solution X has a pH of 3, and Solution Y has a pH of 5. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: Solution X has a hydrogen ion concentration 100 times greater than Solution Y.
choices.B: Solution X has a hydrogen ion concentration 2 times greater than Solution Y.
choices.C: Solution Y is more acidic than Solution X.
choices.D: Solution Y has a hydrogen ion concentration 100 times greater than Solution X.

questions.explanation: The pH scale is logarithmic: each one-unit drop means a tenfold increase in hydrogen ion concentration, so a 2-unit difference is 10 × 10 = 100 times. The lower pH (X) is the more acidic solution. Choice B treats the scale as if it were linear.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

choices.A: The patient's fever had broken, however, she still felt weak.
choices.B: The patient's fever had broken however; she still felt weak.
choices.C: The patient's fever had broken; however, she still felt weak.
choices.D: The patients' fever had broken; however she still felt weak.

questions.explanation: When a conjunctive adverb such as "however" joins two independent clauses, use a semicolon before it and a comma after it. Choice A is a comma splice, and choice D uses a plural possessive for one patient and omits the comma.

questions.stem: Which verb correctly completes the sentence? "Each of the nurses on the night shift ___ responsible for checking the crash cart."
questions.explanation: The subject is "Each," which is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is." The plural noun "nurses" sits inside a prepositional phrase and does not control the verb, which is the trap in choices A, C, and D.

questions.subtopic: Using Language & Vocabulary to Express Ideas
questions.stem: Which word correctly completes the sentence? "The new medication had no noticeable ___ on her blood pressure."
questions.explanation: A noun is needed after "no noticeable," and "effect" is the noun meaning a result. "Affect" is usually a verb meaning to influence, so choices A and B do not fit.

questions.subtopic: Using Language & Vocabulary to Express Ideas
questions.stem: Based on its prefix, the term "bradycardia" describes a heart rate that is
questions.explanation: The prefix "brady-" means slow, and "cardi" refers to the heart, so bradycardia is a slow heart rate. Choice B confuses it with "tachy-," the prefix meaning fast.

questions.stem: Which revision corrects the error in this sentence? "Running to catch the bus, my backpack fell open."

choices.A: Running to catch the bus, my backpack was falling open.
choices.B: My backpack, running to catch the bus, fell open.
choices.C: As I ran to catch the bus, my backpack fell open.
choices.D: Running to catch the bus my backpack fell open.

questions.explanation: The original sentence has a dangling modifier: it says the backpack was running. Choice C adds the true subject ("I") to the opening clause. Choices A, B, and D still make the backpack the one running.
